question: Who helped their teammates more in 2015-16, Curry or LeBron?
answer:
# On-Court Impact Review

## Answer

**My judgement: I lean toward LeBron James.**

**Criterion:** Evaluating playmaking production and on-court team association during the 2015-16 season.

**Decisive reason:** LeBron James generated higher playoff assist volume per 36 minutes and better ball security measured by assists per turnover, supported by a much stronger playoff on-minus-off net rating. This outweighs Stephen Curry's regular season assists per 36 minutes advantage. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Playoffs&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Playoffs&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

**Strongest counterargument:** Stephen Curry held advantages in regular season assists per 36 minutes and on-minus-off net rating, but postseason performance carries heavier weight for overall teammate impact in this comparison. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612744&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/teamplayeronoffsummary?TeamID=1610612739&LastNGames=0&MeasureType=Base&Month=0&OpponentTeamID=0&PaceAdjust=N&PerMode=Totals&Period=0&PlusMinus=N&Rank=N&Season=2015-16&SeasonType=Regular+Season&DateFrom=&DateTo=&GameSegment=&LeagueID=00&Location=&Outcome=&SeasonSegment=&VsConference=&VsDivision=)

**Why this judgement:** Balancing assist volume against ball security reveals a trade-off where raw assist production may be offset by turnover frequency, requiring consideration of both assist rates and assists per turnover ratios.

**What could change it:** Additional tracking data measuring secondary assists or potential assists could alter the relative playmaking evaluation between Stephen Curry and LeBron James.

## Dimension findings

- **Playmaking and ball security:** The indicators disagree; one player does not dominate all selected measures.
- **Team on/off context:** Regular Season: Stephen Curry has the higher on-minus-off net rating; Playoffs: LeBron James has the higher on-minus-off net rating. This describes team association, not an isolated player effect.

This position compares observed contributions, not innate ability. Playmaking uses assists per minute and assists/turnovers, not a complete model of creation. Team on/off is association rather than causation.

**Scope:** 2015-16–2015-16 versus 2015-16–2015-16; Regular Season, Playoffs.

- **Playmaking and ball security / Regular Season:** Stephen Curry (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **7.03** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.01** ratio; LeBron James (2015): Assists per 36 minutes **6.83** per 36 minutes, Assists per turnover **2.06** ratio. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=201939&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- **Team on/off context / Playoffs:** Stephen Curry (2015 / Golden State Warriors): On-minus-off net rating **-2.9** points / 100 possessions, ON min **614** minutes, OFF min **543** minutes; LeBron James (2015 / Cleveland Cavaliers): On-minus-off net rating **19.8** points / 100 possessions, ON min **822** minutes, OFF min **186** minutes.
